about.text: The water-soluble form of casein. Acid casein curd is dissolved in a dilute alkali, usually sodium hydroxide (calcium, potassium and ammonium are also used), and the solution is spray-dried. Sodium caseinate is the most common form, valued as an emulsifier in processed meat, baking and dairy-based foods.

links.name: INFLIBNET (UGC, India): Technology of Milk and Milk Products

how.text: Acid casein will not dissolve in water. Adding alkali takes the pH back up from 4.6 to near neutral, the casein turns into a salt and dissolves, and the solution is dried to a soluble powder used as emulsifier and protein in foods.

steps.name: mill
steps.note: The curd, at 25–30 % solids, goes through a colloid mill to a slurry.

steps.name: neutralise
steps.note: With NaOH 2.5 M (10 %), 1.7–2.2 % of casein solids, or Ca(OH)₂, KOH or ammonia, to a final pH of about 6.7.
Spray dried from a feed of 20–22 % solids to a powder below 5 % moisture.
